analyst_view.overall: Early view: Monza have lost four in a row and Juric was sent off at the end of the 1-0 defeat to Atalanta (the length of any touchline ban was not known when this was written). Monza still had the better of the first half in that game and have Serie A's top scorer in Gustavo Varela (nine goals). Fiorentina are up to 15th after beating Sassuolo and drawing 2-2 with Juventus, but they are missing Parisi (cruciate ligament), Pongracic, Ranieri and Atta, and De Gea's form in goal is under scrutiny.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean higher: Fiorentina's away games have averaged about 4.4 goals and Monza's home games 3.6. De Gea has the lowest save rate among regular Serie A keepers, and Monza, with Varela up front, will attack.

corners.text: The site expects 8.5 corners, and I lean slightly lower. Monza's home games have averaged about eight corners and Fiorentina's away games under seven: Vanoli's side play more directly away from Florence. Many of these teams' chances come in open play rather than from sustained pressure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards, the highest in this group. I lean lower: Monza's home games have averaged about 3.6 cards and Fiorentina's away games about 4.6, so the number looks a little high. Juric's touchline anger does add a risk of bookings.

shots.text: The site expects 28.9 shots. Monza had 22 shots against Atalanta and their home games average about 31, while Fiorentina's away games average about 28, so I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 shots on target. I lean higher: Monza's home games have produced over 12 on target on average, and both sides allow more than 5.5 a game. Varela and Fiorentina's Pellegrino and Njie all take plenty of shots on target.
